name: Convertible Note and SAFE State Machine

positioning.oneLineSummary: Models every note or SAFE as versioned event rules for financing, sale, dissolution, maturity, amendment, and pro-rata outcomes.
positioning.productLabel: Convertible Instrument State-Machine Lens — based on Feld and Mendelson's public Venture Deals materials
notAClaimOf: a valuation cap being a priced-round valuation
all SAFEs or notes using the same conversion base
convertibles being economically simple because documents are short

attribution.display: Based on Brad Feld and Jason Mendelson's public convertible-instrument materials

neutralParaphrase: Treat each convertible note, SAFE, warrant, and side letter as an event-driven contract. Parse cap, discount, interest, maturity, qualified and nonqualified financing, price denominator, sale, dissolution, MFN, pro-rata, amendment, and seniority; then simulate the complete stack in the next financing and downside states.

locator.value: Series index: discount, valuation caps, conversion mechanics, sale, other terms, warrants, and stage dynamics
Chapter 8 convertible debt and alternatives; Chapter 9 cap-table methods with convertible notes
Publisher description: equity and convertible debt among revised legal and procedural topics

requiredConditions: Every executed instrument, amendment, side letter, and version is available.
Each event trigger, price denominator, priority, and holder option is explicit.
The priced-round term sheet and pre-round cap table are available for conversion analysis.
Instrument interpretation and jurisdiction are counsel-reviewed.

requiredEvidence.description: For every instrument: principal or purchase amount, cap, discount, interest, maturity, version, seniority, MFN, pro-rata, warrants, and amendments.
Qualified/nonqualified financing, liquidity, dissolution, maturity, extension, conversion election, repayment, and consent thresholds.
New-money amount, price, pre/post-money method, fully diluted denominator, pool changes, and all concurrent instruments.

decisionQuestions: Which instrument version and exact event rules apply?
Does cap, discount, interest, or another price produce conversion?
What happens in qualified financing, small financing, sale, dissolution, and maturity?
How do MFN, pro-rata, warrants, and side letters change results?
What is the combined ownership and payoff of the complete stack?
positiveSignals: Every instrument and amendment is present.
Event rules and denominators are unambiguous.
Pre-money and post-money instruments are distinguished.
All instruments convert in one deterministic cap-table model.
Sale and dissolution outcomes are separately modeled.
redFlags: A cap is called the company's valuation.
SAFE version or pre/post-money form is unknown.
Only the lowest cap is considered.
Interest, MFN, pro-rata, warrants, or side letters are omitted.
Conversion is calculated instrument by instrument without stack interaction.
disconfirmingEvidence: An amendment or MFN election changes economic terms.
The financing does not meet the qualified threshold.
The instrument uses a different company-capitalization definition.
A maturity, sale, or dissolution state occurs before the priced round.
Consent or majority amendment changes the stack.
contraindications: Do not infer instrument behavior from SAFE or note label.
Do not treat a cap as priced valuation.
Do not calculate an incomplete stack.
Do not let the LLM perform conversion math.

instructions: Inventory every instrument, version, amendment, and side letter.
Encode event triggers, price rules, priority, options, and consents.
Reconcile the next-round denominator and new-money terms.
Simulate financing, sale, dissolution, maturity, and no-financing states.
Show holder-level ownership, payoff, and unresolved counsel interpretations.

sourceReliability.low: Only aggregate convertible amount or cap summary is available.
sourceReliability.medium: Core instruments exist but one amendment, side letter, or event term is incomplete.
sourceReliability.high: All executed instruments, versions, amendments, rights, and counsel review reconcile.

evidenceStrength.low: No complete conversion state can be reproduced.
evidenceStrength.medium: Main financing state is reproducible but one downside or consent state is uncertain.

evidenceCoverage.low: Only amount and cap are known.
evidenceCoverage.medium: Cap, discount, and financing are covered but sale, maturity, MFN, or side rights are partial.
evidenceCoverage.high: All terms, instruments, versions, states, consents, and round interactions are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.low: Instrument type or version is unknown.
applicabilityConfidence.medium: The instrument maps with custom drafting.
applicabilityConfidence.high: Every instrument and state is explicit.

judgmentConfidence.medium: A bounded conversion range is usable.
judgmentConfidence.high: Ownership and payoff are reproducible across states.

promotionRequirements: Venture-counsel review by supported instrument and jurisdiction.
Golden-case tests for mixed note/SAFE stacks.
Complete fourth-edition convertible and cap-table chapter review.
empiricalQualifications: Instrument forms and definitions evolve over time.
Small textual changes can materially alter conversion.
Side letters and majority amendments can create holder-specific outcomes.

rights.notes: Public framework is neutrally paraphrased; only executed instrument text controls.

openIssues: Build event-ordering and consent test suite.
